issues.body: The new text says distinctness does not rest on VALUE_NONE and that datatype routing alone separates degenerate and real value components. But research/zk-field-native-encoding.md section 14.1 explicitly requires VALUE_NONE to be outside the complete reachable handle band, including signed field encodings, with host and Noir assertions; it says this defense remains required even though current fail-closed routing separates datatype constants. The implementation still uses VALUE_NONE = 2, which lies inside the documented [0, 2^64) reachable band. Thus the skill now presents a disputed relaxation as a resolved design fact while the relevant audit record requires the opposite invariant. The scoped routing test only proves current routing and the two unrouted boolean values; it does not prove the audit record's cross-lane reserved-tag invariant.
issues.fix_hint: Either retain the section 14.1 invariant and avoid claiming that routing supersedes it, or update the design/audit record in the same reviewed change with a sound argument for retiring that obligation and consistent host/circuit tests. Do not describe Q1 as resolved while the authoritative record still mandates an out-of-band VALUE_NONE. Keep README wording consistent with that resolution as well.
issues.title: Collision rationale contradicts the audit record's required VALUE_NONE invariant

verdict.summary: The documentation is careful about the research-grade and external-audit posture, and the cited seam is reflected by the real routing test. However, the new collision rationale contradicts the controlling encoding design record's explicit reserved-tag invariant. The PR must reconcile that inconsistency before presenting the revised rationale as resolved.
